verdict.line: You lose extended trades into her Q/E rotation before level 6; you win once Trinity Force comes online and you can time R before her W mist is up.

brief.thesis: Gwen's Q (Snip Snip!) puts true damage on anything standing in the center of her cone and her passive (A Thousand Cuts) heals her off every auto, so every prolonged melee exchange bleeds in her favor before items. The matchup swings on whether you can land R (The Hextech Ultimatum) on her before she reacts with W (Hallowed Mist), because once that mist is up she can only be targeted by someone who steps inside it.

theirWindow.when: when Q and E are both up
theirWindow.what: She can snip you for true damage in the center of the cone, dash in with E (Skip 'n Slash) for bonus on-hit magic damage and attack speed, and heal off both with her passive. Back off and force her to walk up instead of meeting her at range.

yourWindow.what: With Hallowed Mist down she's fully targetable, so this is when R actually locks onto her instead of whiffing into an empty mist bubble. Walk her E cooldown first if you can, then commit R plus Q's recast for the delayed bonus damage.

powerCurve.note: Q true damage and passive healing win short trades
E dash still outtrades your melee-only Q
R lets you force fights if mist is down
Trinity Force spike outclasses her stats

start.why: 51.7% win rate over 151 games and it directly answers Gwen's poke-and-heal pattern — the regen and damage reduction blunt her Q true damage center and passive sustain before you have any items.

boots.why: 52.1% win rate over 290 games; Gwen is a pure magic damage dealer, so the MR from Treads shrinks both her Q snips and her passive's bonus damage all lane.

core.why: Your level 9-11 spike — the stats push you from losing trades to winning them outright, matching the highest-win-rate build path (58.3% over 96 games).
Sustain and AoE damage that lets you win the extended fights Gwen's passive was previously winning.
Damage reduction and healing that directly offsets her Q/passive poke-and-heal loop in the late game.

situational.when: she is out-damaging you purely with magic damage and you need a shield spike
you need more raw survivability to close the gap and land R
you are ahead and want to shorten your R and Q cooldowns to chain all-ins

runes.keystoneWhy: This is a defensive-shape matchup (46.8% win rate, 22.4% pick rate for this page) — Grasp's proc heal offsets Gwen's Q poke and passive sustain in every short trade, which is exactly the exchange you're otherwise losing.

summoners.why: Highest-win-rate combo in the data (51.5%) for this matchup. Since Gwen has the early lane edge, Teleport lets you play the freeze/scale game and reset off poke without giving up wave state, while Flash covers you when you commit R and need to guarantee the stick or the escape.

playing.title: Refuse melee trades under level 6
playing.detail: Any prolonged auto exchange lets her Q center hit you for true damage and heals her off the passive. Trade only when her E (Skip 'n Slash) is on cooldown so she can't dash in and refresh attack speed on you.

playing.title: Bait W before you commit R
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist makes her untargetable to anyone outside the mist, so a blind R can whiff. Wait for her to burn it defensively, or walk into the mist yourself before locking on.

playing.title: Use W's outer edge, not the center
playing.detail: Tactical Sweep slows and deals extra damage in the outer half while healing you regardless of where it lands, so aim for poke range rather than point-blank where she can just walk through it.

playing.title: Save Hookshot for a wall, not just distance
playing.detail: E only works off a nearby wall, so track the lane terrain before you need it — both to knock her up into a fight and to bail out of one.

playing.title: Delay your Q recast when you can afford to sit still
playing.detail: Precision Protocol's second cast does significantly more damage if you wait between casts, but it's only 325 range, so this only matters once you're already in her face.

playing.title: Play for the level 9-11 Trinity Force spike
playing.detail: You are behind in raw trading power through most of laning phase; the plan is to survive to that item completion, not to win skirmishes at level 3-5.

playing.title: Track her E cooldown before diving in
playing.detail: Skip 'n Slash refunds its cooldown on hit, so if she's landed it recently assume it's coming back fast — don't commit R into a lane where she still has an escape dash up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch (16.18.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing advice are my own read of the ability kits, not sourced from that data.
